title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: A great insurer earns its premium multiple not when the combined ratio hits a cyclical trough, but when its normalized underwriting margin and float compounding still clear the cost of equity by twenty points.
epigraph.author: Insurance Valuation Desk Maxim

web_blocks.title: 7.1 Deconstructing $237.35: The Forward P/E vs. P/B Paradox

web_blocks.html: At the November 16, 2026 close of $237.35, Progressive carries a $137.51 billion market cap. It trades at 11.95x trailing earnings, 14.67x forward earnings, and 3.99x book value [1, 25]. On the surface, those multiples look mixed. Trailing earnings look cheap at 11.95x, a steep discount to the S&P 500. Forward earnings look slightly pricier at 14.67x. Price-to-book looks rich at 3.99x next to P&C peers at 1.99x to 3.03x [21, 22, 23, 24, 25].

Solving that puzzle explains why the stock sits at $237.35. It also shows why the $235.10 consensus target sees flat returns even with 6% PIF growth [4, 25]. First, the gap between 11.95x trailing and 14.67x forward P/E reflects an expected -11.90% drop in forward EPS. Underwriting margins are cooling from their FY2025 peak. In FY2025, Progressive posted an 87.4% combined ratio (12.6% margin) and $3,583 million in investment income. That drove $11,308 million in net income and a 35.3% ROE [1, 2, 5]. Progressive runs to a 96.0% combined ratio ceiling. With GEICO and State Farm advertising again, the market expects Progressive's combined ratio to rise from 87.4% (88.7% in Q3 2026) toward 91%–92% [1, 4, 10, 16].

Second, the 3.99x price-to-book multiple is not speculative hype. It reflects a 33.24% trailing ROE and 27.75% ROIC [1, 25]. In insurance, fair price-to-book follows the residual-income formula: P/B = (ROE - g) / (Ke - g). Assume a 9.5% cost of equity (Ke) and 4.5% terminal growth (g). A normalized 24%–25% ROE—from a 91%–92% combined ratio rather than FY2025's 35.3% peak—supports (0.245 - 0.045) / (0.095 - 0.045) = 4.00x book. At 3.99x book, the market already discounts ROE from 33.24% to ~24.5%. It also values the $97.37 billion bond portfolio and $13.50 variable dividend capacity at 14.67x normalized earnings [1, 7, 11, 25].

web_blocks.takeaway: At $237.35, the market pays 14.67x normalized earnings and 3.99x book for a franchise earning 24%–33% ROE across normal cycles—leaving only +10.4% upside to our $262.00 Base target at CMP.

web_blocks.title: 7.2 Excess-Return & Reverse DCF Model: What Is Baked Into $237.35?

web_blocks.html: Standard EV/EBITDA and industrial DCF models fail for insurers. Float is an operating liability, and debt is low at $6,896 million (0.23x equity). We value Progressive with a two-stage Excess-Return model on tangible equity, plus a Reverse DCF [1, 7, 25]. At $237.35 ($137.51 billion market cap), implied book equity is roughly $34.46 billion ($137.51B / 3.99x). Investors pay $103.05 billion above book value for future excess returns above the cost of equity [7, 25].

To anchor our Base Case in Q3 2026 reality, we calibrate growth to recent deceleration. In Q3 2026, net premiums written slowed to +4% YoY and net premiums earned slowed to +5% YoY [4]. We model a 5.5% NPE CAGR over the 10-year window (FY2027–FY2036), rather than extrapolating the 2023–2025 rate-hike surge. We pair that 5.5% NPE growth with a 91.5% normalized combined ratio (8.5% margin), 410 bps worse than FY2025's 87.4%. Assume a 9.5% cost of equity (4.25% risk-free rate, 5.25% equity risk premium, ~1.0 beta) and 4.5% terminal growth. Pairing that underwriting profit with a 4.1% yield on a $100B+ bond book produces a ~24.8% average ROE [1, 2, 7]. Under those disciplined inputs, Base intrinsic value is **$262.00 per share** (+10.4% above $237.35). At CMP, +10.4% upside does not clear our hurdle against a $205.00 stop. That makes $237.35 a `WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT` setup, not a chase.

web_blocks.takeaway: At 5.5% NPE CAGR and a 91.5% combined ratio, fair value is $262.00 (+10.4% vs. $237.35 CMP). That leaves too thin a margin of safety at market, requiring a pullback into $218.00–$226.27.

web_blocks.title: 7.3 Peer Benchmarking: Why Progressive Commands a Book Premium

web_blocks.html: Comparing Progressive to four U.S. P&C peers explains why it earns 3.99x book while peers trade at 1.99x to 3.03x [21, 22, 23, 24, 25]. Chubb ($145.51B cap, $380.84) is a top global commercial insurer. Its capital-heavy commercial lines yield a 15.48% ROE and 12.09% ROIC, under half Progressive's 33.24% ROE and 27.75% ROIC. That gap justifies Chubb's 1.99x P/B and 12.89x forward P/E [21, 25]. Travelers ($82.59B, $402.98) earns a strong 27.50% ROE at 2.85x P/B and 13.00x forward P/E. However, its commercial and property mix carries higher catastrophe and casualty reserve risk than Progressive's short-tail auto core [8, 22, 25].

Allstate ($66.97B, $270.63) posts the highest trailing ROE at 38.92% (29.24% ROIC). It trades at 6.13x trailing P/E, 9.46x forward P/E, and 2.22x P/B after a sharp rebound off depressed equity. Still, its captive-agent cost base and homeowners mix have shown wider combined-ratio swings than Progressive's model [16, 23]. W. R. Berkley ($29.14B, $78.43) trades at 16.60x trailing P/E, 16.21x forward P/E, and 3.03x P/B on a 19.20% ROE [24]. Progressive trades at 14.67x forward P/E—a 9.5% discount to WRB—despite earning 1,404 bps higher ROE. Quality is clear, yet CMP at $237.35 already exceeds the $235.10 Street consensus.

web_blocks.takeaway: Progressive generates 33.24% ROE and 27.75% ROIC—more than double Chubb's ROE—yet at $237.35 (above $235.10 consensus), buyers should wait for support at $218.00–$226.27.

web_blocks.title: Why Street Targets ($235.10) Cap Near-Term Upside vs. $262.00 Base Value
paragraphs: Sell-side analysts value P&C insurers on 12-month forward EPS (14.5x NTM EPS = $235) as combined ratios normalize upward [25]. Even with Progressive's $13.50 variable dividend and $97.37B+ investment float [1, 4, 11], our recalibrated 5.5% NPE CAGR yields $262.00—only +10.4% above $237.35, confirming patience over chasing.

web_blocks.html: Valuation Re-Rating Trigger: Our $262.00 Base fair value drops toward $190.00–$224.80 if Progressive's combined ratio rises above 93.5% or NPE growth slows below 3.5% YoY—or if the stock closes below the $205.00 invalidation stop.

book_subsections.title: 7.1 Solving the Valuation Paradox at $237.35
paragraphs: At first glance, Progressive's valuation at $237.35 looks contradictory. Pull up the stock on November 16, 2026, and you see a $137.51 billion company at 11.95x trailing earnings, 14.67x forward earnings, and 3.99x book value. To a casual buyer, 11.95x trailing earnings looks cheap, 14.67x forward looks fair, and 3.99x book looks pricey next to Chubb at 1.99x or Allstate at 2.22x. Wall Street's consensus target sits at $235.10, slightly below the current market price.

Unpack the underwriting cycle, and every piece snaps into place. The gap between 11.95x trailing and 14.67x forward earnings reflects an expected 11.90% drop in forward EPS. FY2025 was an exceptional year. Progressive posted an 87.4% combined ratio, earning 12.6 cents of underwriting profit per dollar alongside $3.583 billion in investment income. That drove $11.308 billion in net income and a 35.3% ROE. Nobody—not even Progressive, which targets a 96% combined ratio ceiling—expects 87.4% to last forever. As GEICO and State Farm turn marketing back on, the market expects Progressive's combined ratio to drift from 87.4% (88.7% in Q3 2026) toward 91%–92%.

That shift also explains the 3.99x price-to-book ratio. In insurance, book multiples mirror return on equity. With a 9.5% cost of equity and 4.5% terminal growth, a normalized 24.5% ROE justifies 4.00x book value. At 3.99x book, the market has already cut its ROE assumption from 33.24% to 24.5% to price in a 91%–92% combined ratio. That means the easy multiple expansion is already behind us at $237.35.

book_subsections.title: 7.2 Reverse DCF and Excess-Return Reality Check
paragraphs: Standard industrial DCF models fail on insurers because float is an operating liability, not debt. Instead, we use a two-stage Excess-Return model anchored on book equity and a low 0.23x debt-to-equity ratio. Against $34.46 billion in implied book equity, a $137.51 billion market cap means investors pay $103.05 billion above book for future excess returns over a 9.5% cost of equity.

Now let us calibrate our Base Case to Q3 2026 operating reality. In the third quarter of 2026, net premiums written slowed to 4% year-over-year and net premiums earned slowed to 5%. Extrapolating the 15.4% ten-year pace would ignore that slowdown. We therefore model a 5.5% annual NPE growth rate over the next decade. We pair that with a 91.5% normalized combined ratio, which is 410 basis points worse than FY2025's 87.4% peak. Combining that 8.5% underwriting margin with a 4.1% yield on a $100 billion-plus bond book yields an average ROE near 24.8%.

Discounting those excess returns and 4.5% terminal growth at a 9.5% cost of equity gives a Base intrinsic value of $262.00 per share. From $237.35, that represents just 10.4% upside. Compare $24.65 of upside to $32.35 of downside against our $205.00 invalidation stop, and the reward-to-risk ratio at market is only 0.76-to-1. Great businesses are not automatically great buys at any price. Wait for a pullback into the $218.00 to $226.27 support shelf, where reward-to-risk expands to 1.68-to-1.

Our sensitivity matrix makes the margin of safety clear. Hold NPE growth at 5.5% and let the combined ratio slip to 93.5%: fair value falls to $224.80, below today's $237.35 price. If NPE growth cools further to 3.5% at a 93.5% combined ratio, fair value drops to $190.00. Only if Progressive re-accelerates NPE growth to 7.5% while holding an 89.5% combined ratio does value reach our $305.00 Bull target. At $237.35, you pay for strong execution upfront, while a pullback to $218.00–$226.27 puts the odds back in your favor.

book_subsections.title: 7.3 Peer Benchmarking: Quality vs. Optical Multiples
paragraphs: Peer comps confirm Progressive's quality, while also showing why patience pays. Chubb, at $380.84 ($145.51 billion cap), is a top commercial insurer, yet earns 15.48% ROE and 12.09% ROIC—under half Progressive's 33.24% ROE. It trades at 1.99x book and 12.89x forward earnings. Travelers ($402.98) earns 27.50% ROE at 2.85x book and 13.00x forward earnings, but carries heavier casualty and catastrophe tail risk. Allstate ($270.63) posts 38.92% trailing ROE at 6.13x trailing and 9.46x forward earnings, driven by a rebound off depressed equity and a higher-cost captive-agent network.

W. R. Berkley trades at 16.21x forward earnings and 3.03x book on a 19.20% ROE. Progressive trades at 14.67x forward earnings—a nearly 10% discount to Berkley—while delivering over 1,400 basis points higher ROE, Direct scale, and a telematics moat. Quality is never in doubt. Even so, buying at $237.35 above the $235.10 Street consensus leaves too little margin of safety when Q3 2026 premium growth has cooled to 4%–5%.
